question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}36 & 30 \\ 30 & 61\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=9$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=4.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=81,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-81I & =[\begin{aligned}36 & 30 \\ 30 & 61\end{aligned}]-81[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-45 & 30 \\ 30 & -20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-81I)x=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=16,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-16I & =[\begin{aligned}36 & 30 \\ 30 & 61\end{aligned}]-16[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}20 & 30 \\ 30 & 45\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-16I)x=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{27}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{8}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]
$$
